verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's own IAM is documented as controlling who can do what on which resource with fine-grained permissions (google-cloud-docs-7, google-cloud-docs-27). Workload Identity Federation lets workloads reach Google Cloud resources through federated identities instead of service account keys (google-cloud-docs-8), so the least-privilege foundation is first-party. However, the evidence never shows issuing scoped credentials specifically for an agent. missing for 10: documented creation of agent-specific scoped credentials (e.g. service accounts or tokens with narrowed roles), short-lived/scoped token issuance details, agent-oriented guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.
